findings.title: warm_cache causes process termination
findings.description: The function spawns std::threads in a local vector but returns immediately without joining or detaching them. When the vector is destroyed, the std::thread destructor calls std::terminate() if the thread is still joinable.

findings.title: resolve erases valid links and keeps expired ones
findings.description: The condition 'Clock::now() < it->second.expires_at' is inverted. It currently erases links that are still valid and resolves links that have already expired.

findings.title: last_code returns dangling string_view
findings.description: The function returns a std::string_view pointing to a local std::string 'newest', which is destroyed when the function returns.

findings.title: bearer_token buffer overflow
findings.description: std::strcpy is used to copy the authorization header into a fixed-size buffer of 64 bytes without checking the length of the input header.

findings.title: bearer_token null pointer dereference
findings.description: If the authorization header does not contain a space, std::strchr returns nullptr, and the function returns std::string(nullptr + 1), which is undefined behavior and typically crashes.

findings.title: configuration durations misinterpreted as seconds
findings.description: The environment variables LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS and LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS are specified in milliseconds, but they are assigned directly to std::chrono::seconds, making timeouts 1000x longer than intended.

findings.title: prune causes undefined behavior via iterator invalidation
findings.description: Calling links_.erase(it) inside a loop and then performing ++it on the invalidated iterator is undefined behavior.

findings.title: sweep causes undefined behavior via iterator invalidation
findings.description: Calling entries_.erase(it) and then performing ++it on the invalidated iterator is undefined behavior.

findings.title: format_row returns dangling pointer
findings.description: The function returns a pointer to a local stack-allocated char array 'row', which is destroyed when the function returns.

findings.title: check_targets out-of-bounds access
findings.description: The loop condition 'i <= links.size()' allows the index to reach links.size(), causing an out-of-bounds access to the vector.

findings.title: stats causes division by zero crash
findings.description: The calculation 'g_store->total_hits() / g_store->size()' will crash the process if the store is empty (size 0).

findings.title: unchecked query access causes crash on missing parameters
findings.description: The use of req.query.at() in various request handlers will throw std::out_of_range and crash the process if the required query parameters are missing.

findings.title: Cache leaks memory on destruction
findings.description: The Cache destructor calls entries_.clear(), which removes the pointers to Entry objects but does not delete the objects themselves, which were allocated with 'new' in set().

findings.title: require_admin logic is always false
findings.description: The condition 'session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"' is a tautology; it is always true because a role cannot be both 'admin' and 'owner' simultaneously.

findings.title: success_rate uses incorrect integer division
findings.description: The expression 'used / links_.size() * 100' performs integer division first, resulting in 0 for any success rate below 100%.

findings.title: Data race on Store state
findings.description: Store::create and other mutating methods modify links_ and quota_ maps without synchronization. Concurrent requests to the server will result in data races and potential crashes.

findings.title: Data race on Cache state
findings.description: Cache::set and Cache::get modify entries_ and hits_ without synchronization. Concurrent access from request handlers and warm_cache threads will cause memory corruption.

findings.title: Data race on Authenticator state
findings.description: Authenticator::issue and Authenticator::revoke modify the sessions_ map while Authenticator::verify reads it, without any synchronization.

findings.title: Non-atomic Metrics counters
findings.description: Metrics counters (resolved_, created_) are plain longs and are incremented concurrently in main.cpp. This leads to lost updates.

findings.title: Iterator invalidation and race in janitor
findings.description: The janitor thread erases elements from the store's map while iterating over it without a lock. This is a data race against other threads and causes iterator invalidation.

findings.title: Use-after-scope in warm_cache lambda
findings.description: The lambda captures the loop variable 'link' by reference. Since 'link' is a local reference variable, the thread will access a destroyed local variable once the loop iteration completes.

findings.title: Stack-based buffer overflow in bearer_token
findings.description: The function uses std::strcpy to copy the untrusted Authorization header into a fixed 64-byte buffer without checking the length. A long header can overflow the stack, leading to RCE.

findings.title: Arbitrary file write via path traversal
findings.description: The name parameter from the user is concatenated directly into a file path in export_csv. An attacker can use '../' to write files to arbitrary directories.

findings.title: Use-after-free via dangling pointer in format_row
findings.description: The function returns a pointer to a local stack-allocated array 'row'. The pointer is invalid once the function returns, leading to memory corruption.

findings.title: Arbitrary file read via path traversal
findings.description: The read_report function uses an unsanitized user-provided name to construct a file path, allowing attackers to read arbitrary files on the system (that end in .csv).

findings.title: Missing ownership check in link deletion
findings.description: The delete_link endpoint removes a link by code without verifying that the authenticated session owner matches the link owner, allowing any user to delete any link.

findings.title: Administrative access bypass via header
findings.description: Administrative privileges for the /admin/quotas endpoint are verified by checking for an 'x-admin: true' header, which can be easily forged by an attacker.

findings.title: Predictable session tokens via std::rand
findings.description: Session tokens are generated using std::rand(), which is not cryptographically secure. This allows attackers to predict tokens and hijack sessions.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: The /out endpoint redirects the user to the value of the 'next' query parameter without validation, which can be used for phishing attacks.

findings.title: Weak password hashing algorithm
findings.description: hash_password uses a non-cryptographic additive/multiplicative hash (DJB2 variant) which is highly susceptible to collisions and fast brute-forcing.

findings.title: Timing attack in secret_equals
findings.description: The secret_equals function returns immediately upon the first character mismatch, leaking information about the secret via response timing.
